name: Euro-area economy
summary: Euro-area flash composite PMI held at 51.7 in November, a fifth month of growth, though France is weakening
state: The HCOB flash euro-area composite PMI was 51.7 in November, unchanged from October and just below the 51.9 expected, marking a fifth straight month of expansion (Trading Economics, 23 Nov). Germany offset a deepening downturn in France, and business confidence weakened. With the index above 50 and no technical recession or ECB action against bond-spread fragmentation found as of 27 Nov, the signal stays Normal.
for_you: Conditions describe steady but slow growth across the euro area. Firms and workers in France are most exposed if its downturn deepens; exporters to Europe tend to feel weaker demand first.
rubric_hit: Normal: composite PMI 51.7 > 50 and growth positive

sources.title: Trading Economics — Eurozone private sector growth holds steady in November

why: The euro area is the UK's largest trading partner; stagnation there hits UK exports and European markets.
drivers: Energy prices, German industry, ECB policy, fiscal rules, China demand.

rubric.alert: Technical recession, or PMI < 45, or bond-spread fragmentation forcing ECB action.
rubric.normal: Positive GDP growth and composite PMI > 50.
